properties.name: Section 83 - Bighill (US-421 roadcut)
properties.evidence: Cherty and geodiferous dolomite 1.5-5 m thick in basal Renfro; Renfro 16.7-17.5 m (west of projected Locust Branch Fault trend).
properties.position: Carter coordinates 1,800 ft FNL x 1,650 ft FWL, 19-M-64 converted with the KGS Carter 1-minute section grid; position uncertainty roughly 100 m.
properties.citation: Dever, G.R., Jr., 1999, Tectonic implications of erosional and depositional features in upper Meramecian and lower Chesterian (Mississippian) rocks of south-central and east-central Kentucky: KGS Bulletin 5, Series XI

properties.evidence: Renfro 7.8 m on Nada shale; 1.2-m mineralized zone (sphalerite, galena, calcite) 2.6 m below top; 'Platinum Mine' prospect. Evidence of fluid flow along the projected Locust Branch Fault trend.
properties.position: Carter coordinates 2,800 ft FNL x 600 ft FEL, 13-M-66 converted with the KGS Carter 1-minute section grid; position uncertainty roughly 100 m.
properties.citation: Dever, G.R., Jr., 1999, Tectonic implications of erosional and depositional features in upper Meramecian and lower Chesterian (Mississippian) rocks of south-central and east-central Kentucky: KGS Bulletin 5, Series XI

properties.name: Section 95 - Drip Rock (KY-89 roadcut)
properties.evidence: Brecciated dolomite with quartz bodies in the Renfro (northeasternmost reported).

properties.citation: Dever, G.R., Jr., 1999, Tectonic implications of erosional and depositional features in upper Meramecian and lower Chesterian (Mississippian) rocks of south-central and east-central Kentucky: KGS Bulletin 5, Series XI

properties.name: KSPG 2013 Stop 6B - Bighill roadcut, US-421
properties.evidence: 'The upper dolostone bed contains randomly arranged silica (chalcedony and quartz) geodes that appear to replace dolostone.' Uppermost Borden: Nada Member, Wildie Member (commonly mapped as Nada), lower Renfro.
properties.position: Coordinates as published for Stops 6A/6B (37 deg 31' 43.98" N, 84 deg 12' 40.98" W).
properties.citation: Ettensohn, F.R., and others, 2013, KSPG field trip guidebook: The Early-Middle Mississippian Borden-Grainger-Fort Payne delta/basin complex
